(i) for the modified Feldman-Cousins algorithm the coverage is close to the nominal value for the majority of parameterizations and (ii) for the standard Feldman-Cousin algorithm the coverage is below the nominal value for all parameterizations.

(i) the Bayesian treatment of uncertainties is an excellent method to construct confidence intervals in the Feldman-Cousins framework; (ii) the method of integration only in the numerator is preferable to the full Bayesian method; (iii) the coverage of the confidence intervals can be improved by a simple modification of the method of integration in the numerator only; (iv) the power of the method can be increased by a simple modification; (v) the method of combining multiple experiments is very simple and straightforward

the modified Feldman-Cousins ordering with Bayesian treatment gives a better coverage than the original Feldman-Cousinos ordering, that the Bayesian integration in both the numerator as well as the denominator gives better coverage than the modified Feldman & Cousins ordering with Bayesian treatment only in the numerator, and that the Bayesian integration gives better coverage than a frequentist treatment.

the modified Feldman-Cousins ordering with the integration in the numerator only is the best choice for a confidence interval calculation.

the Bayesian treatment of uncertainties is a viable alternative to the Feldman-Cousins method, with the advantage that the coverage and power can be controlled.
